title: Automated Formal Proofs of Combinatorial Identities via Wilf–Zeilberger Guidance and LLMs
claim: A two-stage neuro-symbolic pipeline turns symbolic proof plans into subgoals, then trains a prover on them through verified iteration.
layout: 2 shaded panels, left-to-right, feedback loop with verification gate
description: A wide rounded box titled WZ-LLM holds two tinted panels. The left panel, A. Symbolic Decomposition (blue), starts with a Candidate Statements database icon. An arrow leads to a 'WZ applicable?' diamond. Yes leads to an orange WZ Proof Sketch box (WZ Invariant, Telescoping Summation), then to a purple box of WZ Sub-goals (Boundary obligations, Recurrence lemmas). No sends statements along a lower arrow to a green 'WZ-uncovered IDs' box. The right panel, B. Model Training (pink), shows a Proving Task Pool database feeding a Prover box. A Seed Dataset cylinder feeds the Prover by cold start. Candidate Proofs pass through a Lean Verification Gate. Verified proofs loop back as 'train' with an Expert Iteration cycle. Failed proofs go back via a red dashed line with a red X. DAPO Training leads to a WZ-Prover robot icon.
caption: Overview of WZ-LLM. (A) Symbolic decomposition. Given combinatorial-identity statements, the symbolic engine checks WZ applicability and, when applicable, constructs a WZ proof sketch that is decomposed into sub-goals. Statements that are not amenable to the WZ method are labeled as WZ-uncovered targets. All sub-goals and uncovered targets form a shared pool of proving tasks. (B) Model training. We cold-start a prover with a seed dataset, iteratively generate proofs for tasks in the pool, and verify them. Lean-verified proofs are retained and used for prune/train updates, while unverified ones are discarded. The expert model is further refined with DAPO to yield WZ-Prover for formally discharging both WZ-derived obligations and WZ-uncovered identities.
abstract: Automating formal proofs of combinatorial identities is challenging for LLM-based provers, as long-horizon proof planning is required and unconstrained search quickly explodes. Symbolic methods such as the Wilf-Zeilberger (WZ) method can achieve a mechanized proof of combinatorial identities by constructing special auxiliary functions and demonstrating that they satisfy specific recurrence relations. We propose WZ-LLM, a neuro-symbolic framework that turns WZ proof plans into executable proof sketches in Lean 4 and uses an LLM-based prover to discharge the resulting machine-checkable subgoals. We also train a dedicated WZ-Prover via a Lean-kernel-verified bootstrapping loop with expert-verified iteration, followed by DAPO-based refinement. Experiments show that WZ-LLM achieves a 34% proof success rate on LCI-Test (100 classic combinatorial identities), outperforming strong baselines such as DeepSeek-V3 and Goedel-Prover-V2, and delivering consistent gains on CombiBench and PutnamBench-Comb. These results indicate that our framework provides two complementary strengths: improved direct proving for identities beyond the scope of WZ, and substantially higher end-to-end success when WZ sketches guide a specialized prover.
